[KNOWN PITFALLS — read before writing code]
These are environment/API conventions for this PySCIPOpt harness, distilled
from past failures. Follow them strictly:

1. All data appears in the problem text; transcribe it into
   Python literals ONCE at the top of the script and never
   re-read or reassign the container (e.g. `data = None`
   kills every subsequent data[...] access).
2. m.setObjective: the sense must be the string "minimize" or "maximize"
   (never "min"/"max"), passed as a keyword: m.setObjective(expr, "minimize").
3. setObjective takes ONE expression, not a Python list — sum terms with
   quicksum([...]) first, and never pass a list indirectly via a variable
   (obj = [...]; m.setObjective(obj) also fails).
4. quicksum is a module-level function: from pyscipopt import quicksum.
   m.quicksum(...) and m.sum(...) do not exist.
5. Build comparisons ONLY inside m.addCons(...); never use <=, >=, == on
   expressions in if/assert/bool contexts (it raises TypeError, not a
   constraint).
6. m.infinity is a METHOD: call m.infinity() — passing it uncalled as ub/lb
   raises TypeError.
7. m.setParam only with real SCIP parameter names (e.g. limits/time,
   limits/gap, presolving/maxrounds); never invent parameter names.
8. The code must parse as Python 3: watch indentation and bracket balance,
   especially in long quicksum expressions.
9. PySCIPOpt has NO gurobipy-style attributes: no .ObjVal/.Status/.X/.Pi/.ub/
   .lb/.getLb()/.getUb(). Use m.getObjVal(), m.getStatus(), m.getVal(v),
   m.chgVarLb(v, x) / m.chgVarUb(v, x) instead.

[MODELING PROCEDURE — follow this order BEFORE writing code]
1. UNDERSTAND: one short paragraph — objective and its sense; the decision
   variables; every constraint; and which data fields activate which
   mechanisms (check moq/pack_size/budget_per_period/waste_limit_pct/
   sub_edges/trans_edges/return_rate/labor values in the data schema — a
   zero/null/empty field means that mechanism is INACTIVE for this instance).
2. FORMALIZE: list each decision variable with its domain — CONTINUOUS,
   INTEGER, or BINARY; decide from physical meaning (units of product may be
   continuous; counts of trucks/workers/setups are INTEGER; yes-no decisions
   are BINARY). Then write every constraint as a one-line math statement with
   its index sets, and the objective as a sum of ALL cost/revenue terms
   mentioned in the problem.
3. VERIFY against the problem text: every constraint from the text has an
   addCons, every cost term appears in the objective, every data key you use
   exists in the DATA SCHEMA. Fix any gap, then output the code.

[OUTPUT FORMAT]
- Import: from pyscipopt import Model; import json
- Create the model: m = Model(); silence solver logs: m.hideOutput()
- Set a solver time limit: m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)
- After m.optimize(), print at end:
  st = m.getStatus()
  print(f"status: {st}")
  if m.getNSols() > 0:
      print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
- Output ONLY executable Python code. No markdown, no explanations.

[TASK]
Write a PySCIPOpt script that models and solves the following optimization
problem. All data appears in the problem text; transcribe it into Python
literals at the top of your script.

[PROBLEM]
Implement the selected structured formulation faithfully as a PySCIPOpt script.
Preserve its business variables, objective direction and constraints. Output ONLY executable Python code.

[ORIGINAL PROBLEM]
A factory produces two types of food, I and II, and currently has 50 skilled workers. It is known that one skilled worker can produce $10 \ \mathrm{kg} / \ \mathrm{h}$ of food I or $6 \ \mathrm{kg} / \ \mathrm{h}$ of food II. According to contract bookings, the weekly demand for these two foods will rise sharply, as shown in Table 1-11. Therefore, the factory has decided to train 50 new workers by the end of the 8th week. It is known that a worker works $40 \ \mathrm{h}$ per week, and a skilled worker can train up to three new workers in two weeks (during the training period, both the skilled worker and the trainees do not participate in production). The weekly wage of a skilled worker is 360 yuan, the weekly wage of a trainee during the training period is 120 yuan, and after training, the wage is 240 yuan per week, with the same production efficiency as skilled workers. During the transition period of training, many skilled workers are willing to work overtime, and the factory has decided to arrange some workers to work $60 \ \mathrm{h}$ per week, with a weekly wage of 540 yuan. If the booked food cannot be delivered on time, the compensation fee for each week of delay per $ \ \mathrm{kg}$ is 0.5 yuan for food I and 0.6 yuan for food II. Under these conditions, how should the factory make comprehensive arrangements to minimize the total cost?

Table 1-11

| Week | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
|------|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I    | 10000 | 10000  | 12000  | 12000  | 16000  | 16000  | 20000  | 20000  |
| II   | 6000 | 7200 | 8400 | 10800 | 10800 | 12000  | 12000  | 12000  |

  "direction": "minimize",
  "expression": "sum_{t=1}^{8} [ 240*x1_t + 120*xn1_t + 240*x2_t + 120*xn2_t + 540*x1o_t + 540*x2o_t + 240*s_t + 240*s_{t-1} + 120*xns_t + 120*xns_{t-1} + 120*n_t + 120*n_{t-1} + 0.5*d1_t + 0.6*d2_t ]",

   "x2_t",
   "xn2_t",

 },

  {
   "name": "original_workers_t",

  },
  {
   "name": "orig_in_ot_t",
   "expression": "xo_ot_t <= x1o_t + x2o_t",
   "type": "inequality",
   "source": "original skilled workers in overtime are a subset of total overtime workers"
  },
  {
   "name": "orig_in_train_t",
   "expression": "xns_t <= s_t",
   "type": "inequality",
   "source": "original skilled workers in training are a subset of total trainers"
  },
  {
   "name": "trainee_capacity_t",
   "expression": "n_t <= 3 * s_t",
   "type": "inequality",
   "source": "a skilled worker can train up to three new workers in two weeks"
  },
  {
   "name": "prod_food1_t",
   "expression": "p1_t = 10*40*x1_t + 10*60*x1o_t",
   "type": "equality",
   "source": "one skilled worker can produce 10 kg/h of food I; a worker works 40 h per week; arrange some workers to work 60 h per week"
  },
  {
   "name": "prod_food2_t",
   "expression": "p2_t = 6*40*x2_t + 6*60*x2o_t",
   "type": "equality",
   "source": "one skilled worker can produce 6 kg/h of food II; a worker works 40 h per week; arrange some workers to work 60 h per week"
  },
  {
   "name": "demand_food1_t",
   "expression": "p1_t + d1_t >= D1[t]",
   "type": "inequality",
   "source": "If the booked food cannot be delivered on time, the compensation fee for each week of delay per kg is 0.5 yuan for food I"
  },
  {
   "name": "demand_food2_t",
   "expression": "p2_t + d2_t >= D2[t]",
   "type": "inequality",
   "source": "If the booked food cannot be delivered on time, the compensation fee for each week of delay per kg is 0.6 yuan for food II"
  },
  {
   "name": "training_requirement",
   "expression": "sum_{t=1}^{7} n_t >= 50",
   "type": "inequality",
   "source": "the factory has decided to train 50 new workers by the end of the 8th week"
  },
  {
   "name": "s8_zero",
   "expression": "s_8 = 0",
   "type": "equality",
   "source": "train 50 new workers by the end of the 8th week (training takes 2 weeks, so last start is week 7)"
  },
  {
   "name": "s0_zero",
   "expression": "s_0 = 0, n_0 = 0, xns_0 = 0",
   "type": "equality",
   "source": "no training activity before the planning horizon begins"
  }
 ]
}
